key_insight: Encoding a task-specific spectral query in a data-reuploading quantum circuit can reshape the circuit’s effective hypothesis class without adding new sample-dependent information.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to build task-aligned inductive biases into quantum models when the target problem has known spectral structure, improving data efficiency.
method: Use data reuploading circuits with two inputs: a variable signal and a fixed task-defined query.
Encode the query to modulate how existing signal frequencies are combined, rather than introducing new sample features.
Relate the approach to nonuniform Fourier transform tasks and a radar-inspired classification setting.
evidence_signal: Across small-scale spectral and radar-like benchmarks, aligned queries improved learning from limited data compared with parameter-matched circuits that used mismatched or no queries.
watch_item: The results are demonstrated on small-scale tasks, so scalability and hardware noise effects remain open concerns.
paper_title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
